Experience design notes
Desktop · an answer is only sent with Submit
×
1 · Goal

Give students a clear, low-error, self-paced flow when answering on a classroom display or a tablet. Core rule: an answer is only sent when the student taps Submit, and the app then jumps to the next unanswered question.

2 · Scenario

A student (Emma Lin) answers during Ms. Smith’s lesson: 20 questions, a mix of drawing and multiple choice.

3 · Layout

Top: logo, class info, notifications, avatar (account menu: Class QR code / Leave lesson / Language / Sign out). Left: question list (type icon + status dot). Centre: the answer canvas. Bottom: Skip / Submit answer.

4 · Question types

Drawing: the question image carries ①②③④ markers; tools are pen, text, shape, image, eraser, undo / redo, clear, zoom (Fit) and pan — the canvas stays fixed while the content zooms.
Multiple choice: a zoomable question image plus options A–D; a selection still has to be confirmed with Submit.

5 · States

Not submitted / Submitted. After turning in, the screen locks and the student listens while the teacher reveals the answers on the display. Once revealed, choice questions show the result and the correct answer; drawing questions only compare “my answer” with the model answer and are never marked right or wrong.

6 · Key flow

Choose or draw an answer → tap Submit to confirm → jump to the next unanswered question → Submit all (the confirmation dialog lists what is still unfinished) → after turning in, listen to the teacher reveal the answers (no per-student marking is sent back).

7 · Principles

Explicit submit confirmation, low mis-tap risk, clear status feedback, a fixed canvas that prevents getting lost, and automatic pacing after each submit.
